title: operator-credential-boundary-kms-consent-probe-and-audit-sample-policies
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: prevent cross-operator credential surfacing and provide high-fidelity audit sampling for KMS consent decisions. This PR introduces an operator credential boundary that reduces the blast radius when operator credentials are used to interact with tenant-scoped KMS endpoints and folds in an audit sampling policy so we can observe tenant residency consent decisions without flooding the audit pipeline.

Changes in this PR (high-level):
- enforce operator token masking at the auth gateway for any request that touches 'kms:decrypt' or 'kms:wrap' APIs, ensuring operator->tenant credential transitions are explicit
- add a KMS consent probe service which performs non-blocking consent checks against the regional KMS allocator and exports a compact trace to the audit forwarder when consent is denied/ambiguous
- introduce audit sampling profiles (default, elevated, quarantine) configurable per-tenant to reduce noise while keeping coverage for high-risk tenants
- RBAC adjustments: new 'operator:limited-kms-proxy' role and a short-lived delegation flow that requires explicit consent-proof headers
- observability: new metrics (kms_consent_probe.latency, kms_consent_probe.denials, operator_token_masking.count) and a dashboard prototype

Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (https://linear.app/ENG/brief/ENG-923/operator-credential-boundary) - [x] unit tests for token masking and role-checks - [x] integration test exercising probe fallback when regional KMS unresponsive - [x] feature-flagged rollout (- feature flag: feature.operator_kms_consent_probe) - [x] docs update in security/rbac (brief guide in SECURITY.md)

Rollout plan: staged rollout behind 'feature.operator_kms_consent_probe'. Start with internal tenants, then opt-in pilot customers, then enable default sampling profile changes. Canary monitors added to the console for 5% of traffic. If probe latency > 200ms for 3m, fallback to legacy path and emit an alert to SRE.

Backward compatibility: default behaviour unchanged unless the feature flag is enabled or tenant profile explicitly switched. Masking is additive: operators with older clients still succeed but are routed through proxy that injects consent headers (noop for non-KMS calls).

Related: SUP-4421 incident ticket that highlighted operator token leak surface (root cause doc in the ticket).

Maya Chen: Addressed timeout suggestions, added exponential backoff + jitter and explicit 5s circuit timeout in client_http.go. Expanded design doc blurb and added canary rollout notes.

Ariel Gomez: Security review — requested an additional check that operator tokens created before 2024-01-01 are subject to reissuance or token-signed flag; flagged potential edge-case in air-gapped private deployments.

Maya Chen: Added defensive check: tokens lacking 'operator_consent_v2' claim are routed through consent proxy which adds a short-lived delegation token; documented required change for private installer in notes. Responded to air-gap concerns and added a fallback mode that records a warning and skips external probe when installer disabled external callbacks.
